summary: Rabbi Tawil examines the rebellion of Sheva ben Bichri in Shemuel II Chapter 20, detailing the political tensions between the tribes of Yehuda and Binyamin. The class explores the roles of Yoav and Amasa, the tragic fate of David's concubines, and the intervention of a wise woman who prevents the destruction of her city. Rabbi Tawil highlights how this rebellion introduces the concept of splitting the kingdom, a theme that later comes to fruition in the book of Melachim.
questions: Why did the tribe of Binyamin feel slighted by David?
Was Yoav justified in killing Amasa?
Why does the text compare the rebellion of Sheva ben Bichri to the later split of the kingdom?
What is the significance of the wise woman in the city of Abel of Beth-Ma'achah?
